headline: Iran's tanker-mine claims climb to as many as seven; Trump said to be holding off on strikes
summary: The stories that stayed in the briefing most this week: Iran's tanker-mine claims climb to as many as seven; Trump said to be holding off on strikes; Peltola edges up to 49.9% in Alaska as count nears its end; race still uncalled; Carney: U.S. trade deal is closer, but not without a viable auto sector.

top.headline: Iran's tanker-mine claims climb to as many as seven; Trump said to be holding off on strikes
top.what: Iranian forces now say between five and seven tankers have struck mines and caught fire in and near the Strait of Hormuz within about a day, and claim to have shot down a second U.S. drone in two days; none of this has been independently confirmed. Reuters-sourced reports say President Trump has told advisers he may hold off on attacking Iran unless there are new provocations.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Peltola edges up to 49.9% in Alaska as count nears its end; race still uncalled
top.what: Alaska counted more ballots on Saturday, leaving Democrat Mary Peltola at about 49.9% against Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan's 46% in the last uncalled U.S. Senate race, a fraction short of the 50% needed to win outright. The Associated Press has already called Alaska's governorship for Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Carney: U.S. trade deal is closer, but not without a viable auto sector
top.what: Speaking in Manila on Saturday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said talks with Washington are making progress and a two-country deal is possible, but that Canada is not there yet. He said he will not sign any agreement that fails to keep Canada's auto industry viable.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada and the Philippines finish free-trade talks; signing targeted for 2027
top.what: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced in Manila on Saturday that negotiations on a Canada-Philippines free trade agreement are complete, with both sides aiming to sign it next year. Ottawa also says talks on a wider deal with the Southeast Asian bloc are substantially concluded, though that agreement is not yet final.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Washington plays down Zelenskyy's account of a Donbas-for-NATO idea
top.what: After Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. negotiators asked whether Ukraine would leave the eastern Donbas region in exchange for joining NATO, a U.S. official said many ideas are under discussion and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said questions about Europe's security set-up should wait until the war is over. European Union leaders agreed that Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, with EU officials, will represent Europe in future talks.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Ontario plans OSAP caps and online-program ban for private career colleges
top.what: Colleges Minister Nolan Quinn on Thursday outlined legislation that would limit how fast OSAP-funded enrolment can grow at private career colleges and cut off student aid for programs taught mainly online. The bill is expected to be tabled Monday.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Democratic senator says Lutnick 'must go' as Republican unease over Nvidia scandal grows
top.what: Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to leave over delayed export curbs on an Nvidia customer, and Republican Sen. John Curtis questioned whether the department is acting in Americans' interest. There is no sign that President Trump has withdrawn his support.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Ousted Muskoka chair 'deeply disappointed' as backlash to Ford's regional picks grows
top.what: A day after Ontario named eight regional heads with 'strong chair' powers, Muskoka's replaced chair Jeff Lehman voiced his disappointment and Markham's mayor kept up criticism of Steven Del Duca's York appointment.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.
